# Best Fitness Gifts 2026: 12 Holiday Gifts for Every Type of Fitness Lover


Last updated October 2026


The best fitness gift is the one they're still playing in February.


**Short answer:** The best fitness gifts fit how the person already likes to move, and give them a reason to keep going once the holiday glow fades. For a big gift, match the machine to the person: the Strong Series Rower for anyone who has quit cardio before, the Podium Treadmill for runners, the Summit for hikers, the Justice for small spaces and the Fit Bike S for spin-class fans. For smaller gifts, the Abs Hero core trainer, the Aviron Pulse heart rate monitor and a cozy hoodie-and-thermos bundle all go over well.


Shopping for a fitness lover is harder than it looks, because they already own the water bottle and have strong opinions about leggings. The big gifts carry their own worry: what if it's an expensive clothes rack by February?


Below are 12 gifts, each matched to a type of fitness lover, from solo runners to whole households sharing one machine. Full disclosure: Aviron makes everything on this list, so we'll also tell you who each gift isn't right for.

## How Do You Pick a Fitness Gift They'll Actually Use?


Before you buy, answer three questions:


- **How do they already like to move?** Give them a better version of the workout they already do. A runner will use a better treadmill; a rower they never asked for is a gamble.
- **Where will it live?** Measure first. The Strong Series Rower stands upright in a 35" x 27" footprint, the Justice folds to 53" x 34", and the Summit doesn't fold at all.
- **What brings them back on day 30?** This is what decides whether the gift gets used.


[Research going back to the 1980s](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7721601/) estimates that roughly half of people who start a structured exercise program drop out within about six months. And a[review of 24 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25921307/) found that how good exercise feels while you're doing it predicts how active people will be later on. So pick something that's fun while they're doing it.


Every machine on this list runs[Aviron World](https://www.avironactive.com/workouts/) , which builds game psychology (points, streaks, levels, leaderboards and live races) into science-backed games, coached classes, scenic routes and multiplayer workouts. Streaming apps like Netflix and YouTube are built in too. It's a big reason **92% of Aviron members are still working out a year later** .


A fitness gift can read as a hint, so make sure it's something they already want. If you're not sure, ask their partner, or make it a gift for the whole household.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is a good gift for someone who goes to the gym?


Something that makes the workouts they already do better or easier to fit in. Small upgrades like a heart rate monitor, sweatproof headphones or a weighted vest are reliable picks. If they're often too busy to get to the gym, a home machine they enjoy, like a rower or treadmill with games and classes built in, saves the commute entirely.


### Is fitness equipment a good gift?


Yes, if it matches something they already enjoy or have asked for. Equipment given as a hint is more likely to end up unused. Choose a machine for their favorite kind of workout with something on it to keep them interested, and buy from a brand with a risk-free trial in case it isn't the right fit.


### What do you get a fitness lover who has everything?


Go for an upgrade they wouldn't buy themselves, like a treadmill that hits 14 mph and climbs to 18% for a runner, or one that climbs to 42% for a hiker. If their home gym is already full, a gamified plank trainer like the Abs Hero or a cozy recovery bundle will still feel new.


### What should you put in a fitness gift basket?


Pair a useful piece of gear, like a heart rate monitor or workout headphones, with comfort items such as an insulated water bottle and a soft hoodie. A handwritten coupon for a workout date is a nice finishing touch. For a bigger centerpiece, add a weighted vest or a set of adjustable dumbbells.
